summary: Under construction

Let’s shake up the way we live! A creative adventure, where adelphity, poetry, and robustness shine through.

Hagrou is a collective of citizens united by a shared dream: to rethink housing in Brussels to make it more inclusive, more humane, and more connected to its environment.

Our goal? To relearn how to live together, promoting sharing in both everyday life and architecture. We envision a living space where common areas have their rightful place: a community room open to residents and the neighborhood, a shared laundry room, guest rooms for friends, a collaborative workshop…

Our approach aims to go beyond simple coexistence: no longer just living side by side, but truly together.
title: A cohousing project in Brussels

What should a candidate for the Hagrou adventure know about you? #An introvert who loves words that reflect the world; I listen to them and play with them passionately… before recharging my batteries by reading in the garden in a pink sequinned skirt, (poorly) hidden behind large sunglasses.
Why did you choose to live in a co-housing community (with Hagrou)? #I’d be quite tempted to go and hide away in the forest, near a river where I could swim and among rocks from which to gain a bit of height, but I’d soon feel melancholic and lonely there. Brussels allows me to stay connected in various ways to a humanity that I find beautiful, because it is full of creativity and hope. I dream that Hagrou, whilst broadening my social horizons, will weave even more tightly those bonds of affection that nurture the capacity for self-reflection and resilience.

content:
The collective is organized into working groups that aim to achieve specific objectives validated by the group. Each working group is autonomous and regularly presents its progress and seeks validation from the collective according to a consent decision-making process. Certain decisions are made by consensus (inclusion of members, long-term financial issues, and ethical/fundamental issues).
Following the adoption of the charter, work was carried out to refine the governance and legal structure of the organization.
Our governance? Shared, obviously #We have chosen shared governance as the organizational model for how the group operates. While some groups work with leaders (elected or not) and assemblies that deliberate and make decisions, shared governance is based on the principle that every member is sovereign, with power distributed equally among all.
Hagrou chose shared governance to ensure that power remains distributed equitably and that no individual or subgroup has more influence than another. This seems to us today to be the structure best suited to our values. This is closely linked to the concept of resilience, which is very important to us: unhealthy power dynamics are natural among humans, and we wanted to prevent them as much as possible. Since shared governance offers many tools that suit us, it was natural to move toward this mode of operation.
We use shared governance methodologies at several levels:
Decision-making (consent and consensus) Meeting facilitation (election of facilitators and secretaries without candidates) Task distribution (operating through working groups) Transparency of everyone’s work (work channels open to everyone) etc. Hagrou’s legal structure #We are currently working on defining the legal structure. This page will be updated later.

You want to join the Hagrou adventure? We are always looking for new members to help build the project and live at the chosen location, hopefully from early 2028 onwards (for more information about the location, visit this page).
What is the process for joining Hagrou?
Write to us at hagrouu@proton.net telling us a little about yourself and why you are interested in the project! We will invite you to a presentation of the project. If you are interested in the project, we will invite you to our meetings as a guest member (once every 2 to 3 weeks) and share more details about the project with you. To ensure you are well supported, a pair of buddies will make sure that your integration into the collective goes smoothly: you can ask them any questions you may have! Once you have attended five meetings, if you confirm your wish to join the project, the collective will decide by consensus on your integration.

content:
The Hagrou adventure is currently at the project stage: we are a collective that is preparing to build a future common residential space.
We have identified a site in Schaerbeek and we are proceeding with the design phase, obtain planning permission, and finally renovate! If the project goes ahead, we hope to be able to move in at the beginning of 2028.
The collective housing will consist of three buildings connected by a green space for residents (greenhouse, chicken coop, pond, children’s playground… still to be decided!). In addition to individual apartments, the site will include a large multipurpose room open to the public on an occasional basis, social and craft rooms, guest rooms, bicycle storage, a laundry room for shared washing machines, etc.
The project aims to create 16 housing units, and we are not yet full! If you would like to join the adventure, click here :)

What should a candidate for the Hagrou adventure know about you? #After two years in Brussels, where I joined Hagrou, I’ve been in Montpellier since mid-2026, where I continue to be part of the adventure remotely. I enjoy cultural outings, board games, travelling by train to visit my friends, I do dance classes and my goal this year is to keep my plants alive!
Why did you choose to live in a housing collective (with Hagrou)? #After living for many years in shared flats or as part of a couple, I finally had to face the facts: I love living with people I get on with, but I also need my own space and my independence. Collective living therefore emerged as the perfect solution, and when I came across Hagrou, I recognised myself in all its values: sharing, solidarity, kindness, environmental awareness, creativity, playfulness, and so much more!

content:
The aim of this summary of the charter is to make it easier to learn about the project. It is aimed in particular at external parties, family and friends, partners, and anyone interested in joining Hagrou. It provides a quick overview of the collective’s values, intentions and key principles. However, it does not replace the full charter, which remains the reference document: it sets out our ideas in greater detail, explains the choices underpinning them and describes more specifically how the collective operates. Why this charter? #This charter sets out the vision that guides our co-housing project. It is not a detailed set of rules, but a shared framework that guides our choices and the way we live together.
Our project is based on three complementary pillars:
siblinghood, which places solidarity, inclusivity and care for relationships at the heart of community lif; poetry, understood as a creative and joyful way of inhabiting the world; robustness, which aims to build a community capable of enduring, adapting and caring for its environment. Siblinghood Making solidarity the foundation of living together Our observation #Our societies often encourage individualism, competition and isolation. Social, economic and cultural inequalities make it difficult to forge lasting bonds and foster mistrust towards others.
We wish to explore a different way of living, based on trust, cooperation and the recognition of differences.
Our aspiration #Siblinghood refers to a form of solidarity that encompasses both fraternity and sorority, whilst transcending gender identities.
We want to build a welcoming community where everyone can be fully themselves whilst contributing to a collective project. We believe that diversity is a source of richness: it fosters creativity, the stability of the group and its ability to evolve.
In practice #Our collective aims to:
operate in a horizontal and participatory manner; make decisions through dialogue, consent and the pursuit of consensus; promote transparent and supportive communication; view disagreements as opportunities to learn rather than as failures; maintain a balance between individual autonomy and collective life; pool knowledge, skills and certain material resources; to strive for fairness rather than strict equality, taking into account the realities and needs of each individual; to promote inclusion, accessibility and diversity within the group; to embed the project within its neighbourhood and develop links with its social environment. We believe that everyone is responsible, according to their abilities, for looking after themselves, expressing their needs, maintaining caring relationships with others, and contributing to the life of the collective.
Poetry Living in the world with creativity Our observation #Living together is not just about sharing a building: it is also about building a shared narrative.
In a society that values efficiency, speed and one-size-fits-all solutions, we wish to preserve spaces where people can imagine, experiment, play and create.
Our aspiration #We use the word poetry in its original sense: that of creation.
We want to make our home a place where art, culture, play, humour, imagination and sensitivity play an important role, not as secondary activities, but as ways to better understand the world, to strengthen bonds between people and to invent new ways of living.
In practice #We aim to:
encourage communication that is playful, creative and inquisitive; welcome original ideas with an open mind; recognise the value of trial and error, experimentation and collective learning; pay particular attention to the aesthetic quality of our living spaces; design communal spaces that encourage interaction, creativity, knowledge-sharing and mutual support; ensure that these spaces can, where appropriate, host activities open to the wider community. We want our homes to remain vibrant places, capable of evolving alongside the people who live there.
Robustness Building a sustainable community Our observation #Dominant economic models often prioritise performance, specialisation and short-term growth. This approach undermines both individuals and ecosystems.
We, on the other hand, wish to develop a project capable of enduring through diversity, cooperation and adaptability.
Our aspiration #For us, robustness is not about constantly improving performance, but about building a community that is sufficiently diverse and united to cope with change, the unexpected and future challenges.
Robustness is based on human connections, the sharing of responsibilities and the responsible use of resources.
In practice #We aim to:
foster informal moments of camaraderie and celebration; welcome new members thoughtfully and with care; develop partnerships with the local neighbourhood, associations and other groups; share responsibilities so that the running of the project never depends on a single person; prioritise architectural choices that are sustainable, adaptable and environmentally friendly; promote shared spaces and a ‘use-based’ economy rather than individual ownership; encourage repair, reuse, low-tech approaches and the circular use of resources; develop spaces that encourage soft mobility, DIY, culture, games, gardens and collective projects; document the history of the project in order to share its experience, lessons learnt and the stories that will emerge from this shared adventure. In conclusion #Hagrou is a collective experiment.
We aim to build a community where camaraderie, poetry, and robustness reinforce one another, so as to make everyday life a space for cooperation, joy and empowerment.
This charter serves as a shared compass. It is intended to evolve alongside the group, in step with our shared experiences and lessons learnt.
